Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, launched a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

According to recent reports, that was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

Danns, a promising striker, has had injury challenges and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Fax machines are whirring as the clock continues to tick towards the transfer deadline, but who does your club need to sign? Let us know in the comments below!

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

Nottingham Forest can confirm Omari Hutchinson has joined AC Milan on a season-long loan deal, with the Italian club holding an option to make the transfer permanent.Everyone at Nottingham Forest wishes Omari all the best for his time in Italy. pic.twitter.com/fSv1uNGh2Y.

According to recent reports, fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

According to recent reports, the German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

In a recent development, leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

It has been revealed that borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

Sources indicate that it is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

In a recent development, this has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

It has been revealed that another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

It has been revealed that as reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

In a recent development, spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

In a recent development, A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Sources indicate that burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A massive year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

According to recent reports, enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

Andoni Iraola has shared an update on the injury sustained by Victor Munoz in Liverpool’s win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The only blemish on a terrific result for the Reds in Belgium was the sight of the Spanish winger hobbling off towards the end of the first half, appearing to hurt his knee when overstretching to try and keep the ball after a surging run into the hosts’ penalty area.

A stretcher had been readied for the 23-year-old, but he was at least able to pick himself up off the ground and leave the pitch flanked by medical staff.

Speaking to reporters after the match, Iraola gave an update on Munoz’s injury, with Liverpool’s number 23 due to go for an assessment to verify the seriousness of the glitch.

The Reds’ head coach remarked (via liverpoolfc.com): “It is the worst part of the game, definitely. He was in a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game had finished.

“It has been a knock on the knee, so now we have to assess him. Then if he presents well tomorrow and it’s just this knock… but obviously it’s very early to tell if there is something more than the knock.

According to recent reports, “In the moment it was very, very painful. After the game, I talked to him and he was a little bit more optimistic.”.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The initial signs from Munoz certainly weren’t good, with the winger on the ground for a few minutes before managing to pick himself up, but this update from Iraola at least paints a slightly better picture for now.

We still have to wait for the outcome of the assessment that he’s due to undergo today before we know how severe the injury is, and how long he’s expected to be out of action.

We can only hope that it isn’t a serious setback for the 23-year-old, who’s looked bright and effervescent in his performances for Liverpool so far and was rewarded with a rare start last night before the unfortunate body blow.

Munoz had been playing well in Brugge, too, with Liverpool Echo reporter Ian Doyle noting how the Spaniard offered a ‘real threat with his pace and a regular outlet down the right’ until he was forced off in the 42nd minute.

Fingers crossed for good news on the winger once the medical assessment is completed.

NFL legend Tom Brady is only likely to buy a tiny minority stake in order to join Clearlake's project at Chelsea.

That is according to former Everton chief executive and ex-Premier League board member Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that the 49-year-old may potentially buy as little as a one per cent stake in the club.

Brady is in talks with the Chelsea hierarchy over a move to invest at Stamford Bridge, a move which comes less than a month after he sold his stake in Championship side Birmingham City.

Wyness believes that Brady is likely to buy a stake in the Blues for a "£50million" investment, and feels that the Stamford Bridge project fits his image well.

Reports have suggested that the American will not gain voting rights from any deal, and is instead likely to serve in an advisory role.

Chelsea's hierarchy has been restructured in the months following Todd Boehly's exit, and a fresh face is now closing in on joining the party in Brady.

Everton’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Goodison Park between 2004 and 2009 and now runs a football consultancy advising elite clubs – believes that Chelsea are a much stronger fit for Brady's image than his previous involvement at Birmingham.

The five time Super Bowl MVP is one of America's most recognisable sportsmen, having previously enjoyed a 22-year career in the NFL.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider's Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained exactly how limited Brady's involvement is likely to be at Chelsea.

In a recent development, "Yeah, Tom Brady. Interesting story this one. He obviously didn't seem to fit very well in Birmingham, did he, in terms of them getting relegated and the whole thing?" He mentioned.

Industry observers note that "It didn't seem a Tom Brady story. But he played his role with Knighthead Capital, so I get it. But look, he sort of does fit the Chelsea mould a bit further.

"Chelsea fits Brady better than struggling with, you know, Wayne Rooney as manager and the whole story. That didn't really fit the Brady image, whereas I think Chelsea does.

"I don't see it being much more than perhaps one per cent at £50m, is the sort of valuation I'd put on it. He also may have to do certain appearances for Chelsea in the USA, et cetera.".

Former Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider on Thursday that Cole Palmer's "embarrassing performances" for Chelsea could get Xabi Alonso sacked in the coming weeks.

The ex-recruitment man believes that the England international has been way below the required level of late, and also pointed towards him sulking after the full-time whistle following the recent defeat to Leeds United.

Brown believes that Alonso is "relying" on Palmer to step up and help his team rediscover their early-season form, but is getting nothing from the 24-year-old right now.

Brown feels that Palmer is a clear difference-maker for Chelsea on his day, but his moments of magic have been few and far between so far this term.

He made seven incredible saves at the MKM Stadium, allowing Oli McBurnie's late brace to make all the difference.

Tzolakis currently leads the way in terms of save percentage in the Premier League this season, boasting 4.4 saves per 90 so far [FotMob].

Interestingly, the Tigers signed him from Olympiacos for £20million, a Greek club owned by Evangelos Marinakis.

King has already suggested to Football Insider that Marinakis will be frustrated, having not decided to bring him to Nottingham Forest in the summer.

Tzolakis is now turning into one of the signings of the 2026-27 campaign, and he may be on the move much sooner that Hull anticipated.

"It was one of those days that you would say, 'He isn’t going to get beat today', this guy," King told Football Insider.

"He seemed to be in the right place at the right time for everything. It was as good a goalkeeper performance as you'll see all season from anybody.

Recent findings suggest that "He was a decent buy, him. What is he? 24? He costs, what, £20million? And to be fair, that's a lot of money for a goalkeeper coming from Greece.

Konstantinos Tzolakis was a MONSTER between the sticks for @hullcity against Brighton 👊 pic.twitter.com/xfgqketvcJ.

According to recent reports, "He certainly looks better than the Arsenal reserve goalkeeper. I think they've got a good chance of staying up, and primarily because they've got a decent goalkeeper who's performing well.".

It certainly wouldn't be a surprise if Arsenal registered an interest in the 24-year-old ahead of the January transfer window.

Fans are not aware of how long Raya might be sidelined for, with Kepa Arrizabalaga filling his spot for the last two matches.

Kepa has not made many mistakes, if any, in that time, but the 32-year-old doesn't exactly strike confidence in the hearts of his defenders.

Tzolakis would be an ideal replacement, but he's unlikely to want to sit on the bench and watch once Raya returns from injury.

Breaking: Daily briefing: Is AI ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Depending on whom you ask, OpenAI’s huge drop of AI-generated proofs last month was either an unprecedented achievement or a catastrophe — or both.
  • Sources indicate that amateur astronomers are turning to AI models to search for worlds outside the Solar System.
  • Recent findings suggest that A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people’s brains identified molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Depending on whom you ask, OpenAI’s huge drop of AI-generated proofs last month was either an unprecedented achievement or a catastrophe — or both. “It’s probably the end of mathematics as we know it,” theoretical physicist Miranda Cheng said at an emergency meeting of the Royal Society. Now Anthropic has claimed a full proof of the iconic Riemann hypothesis. Mathematicians are grappling with what might come next — and say that the field’s tradition of openly sharing early ideas is already coming to an end.

Sources indicate that amateur astronomers are turning to AI models to search for worlds outside the Solar System. AI’s ability to scour the internet for freely available planet-hunting tools, such as those made by NASA, and use them to process massive amounts of data has lowered the barrier to entry for non-specialists, researchers say. But some citizen scientists don’t fully understand how to validate the findings of AI models, says exoplanet researcher Michelle Kunimoto. “There’s been a huge, overwhelming surge of AI-driven papers” that describe relatively low-quality planet candidates, they say.

Reference: Zenodo preprint (not peer reviewed).

Recent findings suggest that A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people’s brains identified molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression. These changes include ‘epigenetic marks’ — chemical tags added to DNA that can affect how genes work. And some patterns occurred only in women. Understanding the epigenetic consequences of trauma could help to explain why some people experience symptoms and respond to treatment differently.

Industry observers note that pakistani military pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali is set to become the first foreign astronaut to visit China’s Tiangong space station. Ali is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese taikonauts. “My first [flight] not only represents myself, but also my country,” Ali told reporters at a press conference. The mission is also a milestone for China’s space programme, which now has the capability to offer such opportunities to international partners, claims foreign-policy researcher Yuxuan Jia.

Sources indicate that in Six Maths Essentials, Fields medallist Terence Tao explains how an understanding of the central principles of mathematics can help us to understand the world — all in fewer than 100 pages. For Tao, these six concepts — numbers, algebra, geometry, probability, analysis and dynamics — are the building blocks of reality, and he describes each principle “with elegant minimalism”, writes biomedical scientist Itai Yanai in his review. “The beauty of Tao’s book is seeing maths through his eyes, describing its spirit as well as generalizing across the discipline.”.

Recent findings suggest that biomedical-ethics researcher Brandon Brown argues that if scientists want to advance in their careers, it’s their own responsibility to make peers aware of their achievements. A panel of Nature readers gave their judgement — read on to see if you agree.

Scientific techniques used to investigate the provenance of historical artefacts also shed light on what early chemists knew. Some analyses of art from 18th-century Saxon and Qing dynasties say that they’re later replicas, because the cobalt pigments are too pure — people didn’t know how to eliminate nickel so thoroughly until much later. But not so fast, write five archaeological scientists. They’ve spotted evidence from a European pigment factory as far back as 1731 that might be “the earliest documented protocol for the selective wet chemical separation of chemically similar elements”. Give these ‘chymists’ from artisanal workshops their due, say the authors.

It has been revealed that rich countries that invest in weather-monitoring stations in places that can’t afford their own will reap the benefits of better forecasts and early warning systems, argues Markus Repnik, a director of a United Nations fund called the Systematic Observations Financing Facility (SOFF). (Nature | 7 min read).

Reference: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and World Meteorological Organization report for SOFF.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03841-2.

As well as all kinds of shenanigans that would be illegal in the real world, players can spot some 60 bird species, along with reptiles, amphibians, fish and mammals.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago.
  • Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025.
  • If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Recent findings suggest that poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

Recent findings suggest that “With Alex, it is clear,” remarked Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”.

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

It has been revealed that A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA.

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his fresh territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

According to recent reports, quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

In a recent development, iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

Recent findings suggest that what damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

Recent findings suggest that it was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Sources indicate that inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm.

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

Industry observers note that there will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

Sources indicate that “I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The crucial thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”.

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS.

We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”.

It has been revealed that we are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the newly introduced Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

In a recent development, andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

It has been revealed that “We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola remarked. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

According to recent reports, “He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”.

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

In a recent development, ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

Sources indicate that “What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil stated. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”.

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 19:19, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 19:21.

Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven is reportedly open to leaving the 20-time English champions on loan during the January transfer window.

Heaven, 20, has made eight appearances for the Red Devils this season, including five outings in the Premier League, but he was an unused substitute against Liverpool on Sunday.

Man United are expected to target a new defender during the January transfer window due to their problems in that area of the field.

The Red Devils have conceded 34 times across all competitions this season, which is the worst defensive record in Europe's top five leagues.

According to BBC Sport, Heaven has concerns over what Man United's current struggles could mean for his development.

Heaven allegedly accepts that current head coach Mauricio Pochettino is likely to turn to more experienced options, as the Red Devils face a battle against relegation from the Premier League.

The Englishman has a contract at Old Trafford until the summer of 2029, but it is understood that he would be willing to leave the club on a permanent basis if the right opportunity arrived.

Heaven is at the moment with the Man United squad preparing for Wednesday's Champions League contest with Portuguese giants Sporting Lisbon.

However, it would be a surprise to see him named in the starting side, or feature off the bench, especially as Luke Shaw has returned to fitness.

Fulham's Calvin Bassey and Brentford's Nathan Collins are believed to be January options for Man United to boost their defensive unit.

Heaven arrived at Man United from Arsenal in February 2025, and he has represented the 20-time English champions on 32 occasions in all competitions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:32 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino suggested the Leny Yoro red card that had such an affect ontheir defeat by Liverpool game was 'unfair' and that their opponents should have been 'punished' too.

Pochettino gave up his job as US national team coach to join United on Wednesday, but any hope of a new manager 'bounce' evaporated after Yoro was sent off inside eight minutes and his team were thrashed 4-0.

It was the joint-heaviest defeat for a latest United manager since Lal Hilditch a century ago, and leaves Pochettino's side second from bottom of the Premier League.

In a recent development, 'So painful, so disappointed,' remarked the Argentine, who blamed the early red card for United's defeat. 'It's not OK to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after eight minutes. Now we can explain everything, but the damage is done – it's so painful.

Industry observers note that 'It's clear that after eight minutes the initiative was in the bin. Do you think that is easy? Even the best team in the world playing in this situation concedes four goals or maybe more.

'We are not going to lose more than one game how we lost today. I take the responsibility, and we keep pushing.

Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino blamed Leny Yoro's red card for his side's defeat by Liverpool.

Yoro (right) was sent off for fouling Alexander Isak inside eight minutes of Sunday's game.

'We feel pain for this defeat, but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger into energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game.

'We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing-room.

'The players are feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

'We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.'.

Pochettino was unhappy that referee Sam Barrott showed Yoro a straight red card for his challenge on Alexander Isak, having taken no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Bryan Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty box moments earlier.

'In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal. Everyone who plays football can feel it,' added the United boss. 'If you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak. The ball was going to the goalkeeper.

Industry observers note that 'If you look before, in the sixth minute, Jacquet on Mbeumo. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty. We were punished badly and they were not punished, that is the truth.'.

He later added: 'One centre-back made a mistake and wasn't punished and us, we made one mistake and we were punished.'.

Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes agreed their team-mate should not have been sent off.

United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo agreed with Pochettino that it wasn't a red card.

Sources indicate that 'No chance,' said Mainoo. 'The ball is already with the keeper, and they're both running full speed. What can he do?

'I feel like the game has been taken out of our hands early by a red card that I don't think can be a red card.

'It's hard but no-one is going to save us. We have to come together and keep digging, keep fighting, and it will come round.'.

Captain Bruno Fernandes, meanwhile, added: 'I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card, and I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR with a long time to see, do it in slow motion, and make a mistake like this which can change the game.'.

Gary Neville, who was left slapping himself in the face in shock live on Sky Sports, was pleased with damage control on, with United conceding four when it looked at one point that it would have been many more.

Former United captain Roy Keane, however, wasn't, and took aim at his ex-side's display.

'I thought United were desperate,' he remarked. 'So bad. Neville's OK with 4-0? Are you telling me they could have done better? 4-0 is not too bad with 10 men? Has anyone ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done.

Roy Keane (pictured), meanwhile, questioned why Gary Neville was pleased with the scoreline.

In a recent development, 'People who played for the club noted 4-0 is not too bad? Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish?

It has been revealed that 'Liverpool were excellent but how easy did United make it for them? This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers. When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making?

'Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying four is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are nicely on course to qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16 after their 3-0 win away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds’ 100% start to the league phase was ended by a 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but they responded to that setback in Istanbul with a thoroughly impressive victory against the Belgian side, with whom they were level on points prior to the match.

That result has left Andoni Iraola’s team fifth in the league phase standings with 12 points from a possible 15, with a top-eight finish seeing them bypass the bear pit of the knockout play-off round in February.

Now that we’re past the halfway mark of the league phase, the 36 Champions League clubs have a strong indication as to where they’re likely to finish, and what more needs to be done to achieve their targets.

According to recent reports, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

At present, Manchester City occupy the final position for automatic passage to the round of 16, with Enzo Maresca’s side on 10 points, averaging two per game.

That means the projected points tally required for a top-eight placing is 16, so Liverpool would need to aim for at least four points from their remaining three matches against Porto (home), Inter Milan (away) and Lens (home).

The two Anfield fixtures are against teams placed 22nd and 34th respectively, so the Reds would be fully expected to win both of those.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

The visit to the San Siro is likely to be much tougher, but LFC beat Inter at the famous venue last season, and a repeat result would probably be enough to guarantee a top-eight finish with one game to spare.

That’d give Iraola the luxury of being able to rest key players for the concluding fixture against Lens, which falls between Premier League matches against Manchester United and Everton.

With Liverpool also still going strong in the Carabao Cup and plausibly making it to a two-legged semi-final in the opening weeks of 2027, any opportunity to rotate the squad in January must be embraced.

The picture can obviously change over the final three matchdays, but right now it seems probable that if the Reds beat Porto and get a result away to Inter, they could be effectively or even mathematically assured of a top-eight finish by the time they host Lens.

That objective is well within reach for Iraola’s side, and avoiding the play-off round in February is a must.

By Saikat Mandal | 24 Nov 2026 19:25, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 06:17.

Union SG will be looking to maintain their impressive Europa League form when they host Lech Poznan at King Power at Den Dreef Stadium on Thursday.

The Old Lady remain unbeaten in the competition and sit fourth in the standings, while the visitors are languishing second from bottom in the table.

The Belgian side began their Europa League campaign with a convincing 3-0 victory over Viktoria Plzen away from home and have since collected 10 points from four matches, scoring 10 goals in the process.

The only occasion on which they dropped points came against Real Sociedad, when David Hubert's side fought back from behind to secure a 1-1 draw.

A scintillating second-half display helped them to a commanding 4-0 victory over Hapoel Be'er Sheva, while Union followed that up with a 2-1 triumph over Celta Vigo on matchday four.

They are unbeaten in their last 16 matches and head into this encounter on the back of seven consecutive victories across all competitions, a run that should give them plenty of confidence.

USG are also setting the pace in the Pro League, sitting top of the table with 32 points from 12 matches, having recorded 10 wins and two draws without tasting defeat.

Lech Poznan comfortably dispatched Swiss side Thun 9-2 on aggregate to secure their place in the Europa League league phase, but they have since struggled to find their feet in the competition.

The Railwaymen began their campaign with a 4-0 defeat to Crystal Palace before suffering another heavy loss by the same scoreline against Bayer Leverkusen.

The Polish side ground out a hard-fought 1-1 draw against Sunderland, but Benfica proved too strong in their next outing, handing them a 3-1 defeat on matchday four.

Having scored just two goals and conceded 12, they are among the three teams languishing near the bottom of the table with only one point, with only FC Ararat-Armenia faring worse.

Lech Poznan, however, have been outstanding domestically, sitting top of the league with 35 points from 14 matches, four clear of Gornik despite having played a game fewer.

Hubert could make several changes to the side that faced Kortrijk in their last league outing, with Nikki Havenaar potentially coming into a three-man defence and Louis Patris moving into midfield.

Besfort Zeneli, who scored twice against Celta Vigo, is likely to return to the starting lineup in place of Darius Olaru, while Kevin Rodríguez is expected to lead the line.

Lech Poznan, meanwhile, are likely to adopt a more cautious approach away from home, with Niels Frederiksen potentially setting his side up in a 4-2-3-1 formation, with Yannick Agnero operating as the lone striker.

Mateusz Pruchniewski has been ruled out for the rest of the season with an ACL injury, while Ali Gholizadeh is still recovering from the same problem and is unlikely to return before January.

Alex Douglas is sidelined with a broken rib, while Joao Moutinho is not expected to return before February. However, Pablo Rodriguez and Mikael Ishak have both returned to training.

Lech Poznan are still searching for their first Europa League victory this season, and although they may have to wait a little longer to break that duck, we expect the visitors to find the net and put up a strong fight.

Nottingham Forest were trying to prove a point by voting against the idea of covering legal defence fees for Premier League directors amid the ongoing saga surrounding Manchester City.

That is according to former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that the Reds were simply making their dissatisfaction known.

Man City's leading sponsors Etihad have threatened to take legal action against the Premier League, with 18 clubs voting to cover the cost of defences for each league director should that scenario play out.

Wyness believes that enough clubs were always going to vote in favour of the idea, leaving Forest with the chance to simply prove their point.

14 clubs had to vote in favour of the idea for the notion to be passed, and Forest and City were the only two clubs who voted against.

The East Midlands outfit have had plenty of run-ins with the league in recent years, including a controversial points deduction back in 2024, and Wyness feels they are just trying to get their own back.

Everton’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Goodison Park between 2004 and 2009 and now runs a football consultancy business advising elite clubs – believes that Forest's vote was always likely to be ineffectual, given the stances shown by the other clubs.

As a result, he feels that owner Evangelos Marinakis used the vote as the chance to make a "protest" against the treatment his club have received in recent years.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider's Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained the likely thinking behind Forest's decision.

"Well, I haven't seen it officially revealed that it was Forest, but I'm pretty sure that all the reports are accurate, so we'll go on that one," he remarked.

"Let's say that, Marinakis must think that the Premier League are an inconsistent referee, is what I would say.

According to recent reports, "And he also claimed that he didn't have enough information. So that's where we are with it.

"Look, I think they've made their protest, and good for them, they've remarked it, so that's the situation, and they were never going to lose the vote so Forest made their point.".

Football Insider revealed on Tuesday that Roma are keen to sign Forest winger Callum Hudson-Odoi on loan in January.

The wideman has been firmly down the pecking order for Oliver Glasner of late, and has played just 45 minutes of Premier League football so far in 2026-27.

Roma are keeping a close eye on the 26-year-old's situation, but are not prepared to make a permanent move for Hudson-Odoi mid-season.

However, a loan move is firmly on their radar at the moment, even though Chelsea's Jamie Gittens presently stands as their first choice target.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 24 Nov 2026 19:40.

Braga will look to strengthen their position in the Conference League knockout-stage race when they welcome KuPS Kuopio to the Estadio Municipal de Braga on Thursday evening.

Franclim Carvalho's side are 17th in the 36-team standings with four points from three matches, while the Finnish visitors sit 33rd with just one point after failing to win any of their opening three European outings.

Despite going unbeaten in their six matches across three Conference League qualifying rounds (W4, D2) and keeping clean sheets in all of them, Braga have found life in the league phase considerably more challenging.

The Archbishops began their campaign with a disappointing 3-0 defeat away to Copenhagen before responding with a 2-0 home victory over Gent on matchday two, giving Carvalho his first win since replacing the sacked Carlos Vicens in October.

However, Braga were unable to build on that success in their latest continental outing, playing out a goalless draw away to Aarhus, although the fresh manager can take encouragement from the defensive improvements made in recent times.

The Portuguese outfit are unbeaten in their last four matches across all competitions, keeping clean sheets in each and winning three, with their latest success coming in a 2-0 victory away to Vitoria de Guimaraes in the Taca de Portugal at the weekend.

That result followed a 1-0 league win at Rio Ave, leaving Braga eighth in the Primeira Liga table with 17 points from their opening 11 fixtures and three points adrift of the top five.

The Archbishops are also three points away from fifth place in the Conference League standings, with several teams between 10th and 14th sitting just two points ahead, meaning maximum points on Thursday could strengthen their hopes of securing a top-eight finish.

Braga have plenty of reason to feel confident ahead of the contest, having won 14 of their last 16 home matches in European competition (D1, L1) and kept 12 clean sheets during that run.

KuPS, meanwhile, have struggled to make an impression in their second consecutive Conference League league-phase campaign, losing 4-2 to Trabzonspor in their opening fixture before suffering a 2-0 defeat away to Borac Banja Luka on matchday two.

The Finnish side collected their first point with a goalless draw against Gent on matchday three, but that result did little to disguise their attacking struggles, having scored just twice and conceded six goals across their opening three matches in the competition.

Miika Nuutinen's men have also gone seven matches without a victory, including a 1-1 draw against Swedish side Norrkoping in a friendly on November 19, while their most recent competitive outing was a 2-0 home defeat to Inter Turku in their final match of the 2026 top-flight campaign.

That result left the Yellow-Blacks third in the Veikkausliiga table, meaning they missed out on retaining the domestic title they won last season but secured a place in the first qualifying round of the Conference League.

KuPS have also struggled on their travels, recording just one victory in their last eight competitive away matches and failing to win any of their most recent four, three of which ended in defeat.

Braga will be without Sikou Niakate, who is recovering from a ruptured Achilles tendon that has kept him sidelined since April.

Jonas Wind is also doubtful after missing the recent victory over Vitoria because of physical overload, while Gabriel Silva returned as a second-half substitute at the weekend after missing the previous four matches through fitness problems and could feature again as he builds up his match fitness.

Fran Navarro ended a more than three-month wait for a goal by scoring against Vitoria and is expected to retain his place at the head of the attack, with club captain Ricardo Horta and Pau Victor also likely to feature in Carvalho's forward line.

KuPS could be without 22-year-old Ghanaian winger Bob Nii Armah, who picked up an injury during the goalless draw with Gent.

Thirty-three-year-old attacker Piotr Parzyszek has started all three of the Finnish side's league-phase matches and could retain his place despite failing to score in his last 10 competitive appearances for the club.

Braga possible starting lineup:.

B Fontes; V Gomez, Lagerbielke, Barisic, Travassos; Gorby, Dorgeles, Moutinho; P Victor, Navarro, Horta.

Kreidl; Savolainen, Hamalainen, Lotjonen, Kujasalo; Gasc, Pasanen; Aiki, Pennanen, Eskesen; Parzyszek.

KuPS have managed just two goals in three Conference League matches and enter this encounter without a win in six outings, while Braga have won three of their last four matches and kept clean sheets in all of them, making a home victory the most likely outcome.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Reds’ number 1 didn’t have his best outing in his previous European game, committing a costly error in the 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but he’s been in terrific form since that aberration in Istanbul.
  • He gave one of his best-ever performances in the recent victory at Crystal Palace and has followed that up with consecutive clean sheets against Manchester United and Club Brugge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alisson Becker made Champions League history in Liverpool’s 3-0 win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds’ number 1 didn’t have his best outing in his previous European game, committing a costly error in the 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but he’s been in terrific form since that aberration in Istanbul.

He gave one of his best-ever performances in the recent victory at Crystal Palace and has followed that up with consecutive clean sheets against Manchester United and Club Brugge.

Not only did he achieve a shutout in Belgium, he also claimed an assist for Alexander Isak’s second goal, with his long kickout finding the Swedish striker, who shrugged off the challenge of Brandon Mechele before finishing neatly past Yann Sommer.

As noted by liverpoolfc.com, Alisson became the first Liverpool goalkeeper to record an assist in the Champions League, with that being the fourth goal he’s set up during his time with the Reds.

It also puts him level with Pepe Reina and Bruce Grobbelaar for assists with LFC, and the Brazilian has achieved it in fewer games than those two.

Sources indicate that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Liverpool fans are no strangers to seeing their number 1 set up an attacking teammate to score, having done so for Mo Salah on three occasions, including the memorable clincher at home to Man United in January 2020.

We’ve even been fortunate enough to see Alisson get on the scoresheet himself with that famous stoppage-time winner against West Brom in May 2021 when Champions League qualification was in the balance.

The assist for Isak was a nice bonus to go along with another strong outing in terms of his core goalkeeping duties, having pulled off a terrific save to deny Felix Lemarechal when the score was 1-0 in the second half and Club Brugge were pushing hard for an equaliser.

As it stands, this’ll be the Brazilian’s final season as a Liverpool player, with his current contract due to expire next June, although his agent is reportedly in talks with club chiefs over a prospective extension.

Considering his ongoing importance to the Reds, we hope and pray that Alisson (still only 34) will agree to stay on for at least another year or two – possibly time enough for him to add more assists to his tally!

  • Seeking to bounce back from a rare Premier League defeat, Brighton & Hove Albion welcome Universitatea Craiova to the Amex Stadium for matchday four in the Conference League on Thursday night.
  • Both teams have identical records in the League Phase, collecting seven points courtesy of two wins and one draw from their first three games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 19:45, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 11:48.

Seeking to bounce back from a rare Premier League defeat, Brighton & Hove Albion welcome Universitatea Craiova to the Amex Stadium for matchday four in the Conference League on Thursday night.

Both teams have identical records in the League Phase, collecting seven points courtesy of two wins and one draw from their first three games.

Following a strong run of six wins and one draw in seven Premier League games, Brighton came away from the MKM Stadium stunned after conceding two stoppage-time goals to lose 2-0 away against Hull City on Sunday.

It has been revealed that head coach Fabian Hurzeler rued his side’s “missed opportunity which can't happen again” after seeing leaders Arsenal and Man City also drop points over the weekend. Brighton still sit between both clubs in second place in the table, six points behind the Gunners and level on points with City in third.

Brighton have scored a whopping 40 goals in 18 games across all competitions this term, but the goals have dried up slightly in recent weeks; they have drawn a blank in front of goal in three of their last seven games and have scored at least twice on just two occasions during this run.

While the prospect of qualifying for next season’s Champions League via their domestic performances has become a distinct possibility, Brighton also have aspirations of winning their first-ever major trophy and following in the footsteps of Crystal Palace, West Ham and Chelsea in winning the Conference League this term.

The Seagulls, who secured a narrow 1-0 win over Getafe in Spain three weeks ago, presently sit fifth in the 36-team League Phase standings and could consolidate their place in the top eight with a victory on Thursday.

Should they beat Craiova without reply, they will become just the third English team this century to prevail in five consecutive European home games without conceding a goal.

Universitatea Craiova narrowly missed out on a place in the Conference League knockout rounds last season, finishing outside the top-24 positions on goal difference after accumulating seven points from six matches.

However, the White-Blues have already picked up the same number of points in half as many games so far this season and sit eighth in the table, leaving them well-placed to secure a historic first-ever appearance in the knockout stages of UEFA competition and potentially bypass the playoff round altogether.

After holding Getafe to a 1-1 draw on matchday one, Filipe Coelho’s side have since celebrated back-to-back wins over Andorran outfit Inter Escaldes (3-1) and Albanian team Egnatia (1-0) – they have not won three consecutive European games since a four-match streak in the 1984 UEFA Cup.

Craiova travel to the South Coast of England in superb form, having put together an impressive 15-game unbeaten run in all tournaments (W11 D4), most recently winning 6-2 against UTA Arad last weekend to retain their position at the top of the Romanian Superliga table.

Sources indicate that femi Azeez was “available” to face Hull at the weekend but was not selected in the matchday squad. The summer signing from Millwall recently recovered from a thigh injury and could be ready to make his long-awaited debut for the Seagulls on Thursday.

Brighton’s Jack Hinshelwood has scored each of his last five goals for Brighton on home soil and could be recalled to the first XI along with the likes of Ferdi Kadioglu, Mats Wieffer, Ibrahim Osman and Charalampos Kostoulas.

As for Universitatea Craiova, Monday Etim (muscle) and Pavlo Isenko (knee) are both ruled out with injuries, while Mihnea Radulescu is ineligible for the Conference League.

Coelho is expected to stick with a 3-4-3 formation, with Oleksandr Romanchuk, Nikola Stevanovic and Vladimir Screciu set to continue in a three-man backline as Nicusor Bancu and Carlos Mora operating as wing-backs.

Stefan Baiaram scored a brace at the weekend and could retain his starting spot on the left side of attack, while Simon Elisor and Assad Al-Hamlawi have both netted 11 goals this season and will battle it out for a start up front.

As the only team yet to concede in this season’s Conference League, and with nine of their last 10 home outings seeing at least one side fail to score, Brighton possess the defensive solidity to frustrate an in-form Craiova attack.

The Romanian leaders are set for by far their sternest examination on the continent, and even if Hurzeler opts to shuffle his pack, the Seagulls should have more than enough quality to claim a routine victory.

‘Already discussing…’ – Fabrizio Romano shares how Liverpool chiefs feel about Andoni Iraola

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (474 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Empireofthekop

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fabrizio Romano has revealed that the Liverpool hierarchy are ‘delighted’ with the work that Andoni Iraola has done so far as head coach.
  • It’s been nearly six months since the Basque was appointed as Arne Slot’s successor in the Anfield dugout, and so far the trend on his watch has been largely positive.
  • The Reds sit fourth in the Premier League table (one point off second) and are on course to once again qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16, while also progressing to the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fabrizio Romano has revealed that the Liverpool hierarchy are ‘delighted’ with the work that Andoni Iraola has done so far as head coach.

It’s been nearly six months since the Basque was appointed as Arne Slot’s successor in the Anfield dugout, and so far the trend on his watch has been largely positive.

The Reds sit fourth in the Premier League table (one point off second) and are on course to once again qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16, while also progressing to the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup.

Including penalty shootouts, Iraola has won 12 of his first 18 games in charge, with just three defeats (two of which came in controversial circumstances against Arsenal and Manchester City).

In a video on his eponymous YouTube channel, Romano spoke of how highly Iraola’s work so far has been regarded at Liverpool, with the head coach already in discussions with club chiefs over transfer prepares for 2027 and beyond.

The Italian said: “They are already discussing with Andoni Iraola about future plans and what they want to do. They are delighted with the coach and the coach is delighted with the Liverpool project. [He has] very good connections with the players.”.

Sources indicate that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Without intending to denigrate the job that Slot did at Liverpool, it seems undeniable that the performance levels of a few players have improved exponentially under Iraola.

Recent findings suggest that alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz have both been thriving in recent weeks, while Alexis Mac Allister has been drastically rejuvenated since the end of last season. With all three of those on song, the Reds’ chances of success should improve considerably.

Iraola notably signed a two-year contract when he took the job at Anfield, which at first may seem a surprisingly short agreement, but it’s one which aligns with how he’s operated at previous clubs.

He’ll know from how dramatically Slot fell from grace in the space of a few months that a glowing reputation now could count for nothing by April or May if Liverpool were to endure a prolonged slump over the winter and into spring.

For now, though, the current head coach has breathed upcoming life into a fan base which was hugely disenchanted towards the backend of last season, and that appears to be recognised by the club’s hierarchy as they give a firm seal of approval to the job that he’s done so far.

Hopefully Iraola continues in the same vein for the rest of this campaign and beyond!

#198465. Industry News: Blend public cash and private innovation to unlock drug development

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1739 w)

Industry News: Blend public cash and private innovation to unlock drug development

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1739 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh model of research and development is needed to incentivize manufacturers to go after diseases that aren’t sure bets.Credit: Stanislav Gvozd/Getty.
  • According to recent reports, for decades, most countries have followed the same model of biomedical innovation.
  • According to recent reports, this approach has generated extraordinary drugs and therapies as well as economic success.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh model of research and development is needed to incentivize manufacturers to go after diseases that aren’t sure bets.Credit: Stanislav Gvozd/Getty.

According to recent reports, for decades, most countries have followed the same model of biomedical innovation. Basic research is undertaken mostly by universities and academia, and private industry leads the translation of research into health solutions1.

According to recent reports, this approach has generated extraordinary drugs and therapies as well as economic success. In 2022, the pharmaceutical sector contributed US$2.3 trillion — or around 1.7% — to global gross domestic product (GDP) and supported 75 million jobs2.

How tech billionaires are disrupting biomedical science.

How tech billionaires are disrupting biomedical science.

However, market failures have been common. Companies have underinvested in developing therapeutics for common diseases with poorly understood biological mechanisms, such as depression, anxiety and kidney disease, because they consider them too commercially risky or unprofitable to pursue3.

To address this gap, we propose an adapted innovation model based on mission-driven public–private partnerships (PPPs), in which government acts as a leading strategic investor. By bringing together the best scientists in academia and industry and lowering risks in industry development in areas of public need and for diseases with limited understanding, this model would accelerate translation, advance health and increase economic returns.

Industry observers note that here, we outline how it would work. It will require systems to ensure affordable access to drugs and therapies, as well as revenue sharing between public and private partners to guarantee public benefits and to support investments in innovation.

Complex diseases that affect swathes of the population create persistent health and economic burdens. Yet, the current biomedical innovation model has proved limited in addressing evolving health needs. Because private investment is guided by assessments of risk and return, it tends to favour diseases with well-defined biological mechanisms and high commercial potential. Diseases that are biologically complex, varied or associated with uncertain markets remain underexplored.

For example, in 2023, more than 300 million people globally had depression. The condition will cost the global economy an estimated $12 trillion between 2025 and 20504. In the United States in 2024, one in five people reported that they had received a diagnosis of major depressive disorder during their lifetime, resulting in an economic burden of $334 billion annually across health-care, household-related and workforce costs5. Yet, the leading drug class for depression (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) has remained unchanged since the 1970s6.

The grand proposal to transform psychiatry — by personalizing mental-health care.

The grand plan to transform psychiatry — by personalizing mental-health care.

It has been revealed that other chronic diseases impose similarly large burdens. For example, chronic kidney disease affects around 800 million people worldwide — nearly one in seven — and is projected to become the fifth leading cause of death globally by 2040 if current trends continue7,8. Yet, existing therapies cannot stem its toll on human lives.

Industry observers note that antimicrobial resistance is another example, which is associated with 4.7 million deaths globally each year and could contribute to 10 million deaths annually by 2050. Increased treatment costs for people with resistant infections amount to $1 trillion every year9. The antibiotic development pipeline has been depleted over time as economic factors render companies’ return on investment lower than that for other drug classes9. These factors include insufficient funding for research and challenging business models, given the short duration of antibiotic treatments and the need to reserve successful upcoming antibiotics as drugs of last resort, to be used after all other options have failed.

Recent findings suggest that bringing a therapy to market from discovery can take 10–15 years and cost anywhere between $880 million and $2.3 billion10,11. The majority (90%) of drug candidates fail after entering clinical studies, clinical trials and drug-approval processes12. And companies won’t invest if they are unsure whether a drug will be profitable.

According to recent reports, consequently, many diseases and conditions have no or few available therapies or only modestly effective options13. What’s needed is a mission-driven strategy to guide scientific capabilities and industry development towards areas of public need by elucidating biological mechanisms and aligning incentives for diseases in which market forces alone are insufficient14.

We propose addressing this misalignment of incentives by reconceptualizing the government’s role in therapeutic advancement through a model of mission-driven PPP. Complementing existing grant-based systems, the model would position the government as a principal investor in select areas of therapeutic development.

The government would thus influence which areas of health and science receive concentrated attention and how successful outcomes are deployed for the public good. Such a model could address specific national needs and global challenges. Here are seven components.

Technicians at work in a pharmaceutical factory.Credit: Getty.

Select disease targets. We propose the establishment of a government-appointed independent advisory body or commission tasked with identifying priority disease targets using transparent, evidence-based criteria, including disease burden, economic cost, scientific readiness and demonstrable market failure. Further criteria to gauge and consider public input into the selection process could be implemented to ensure public trust.

According to recent reports, set up collaborations. A national government, acting alone or as part of an international consortium, would assume a leading role in supporting basic research into biological mechanisms. It would do so by bringing together basic scientists from academia and translational experts from industry to reduce risks in translational development. Private industry would contribute expertise in drug development, clinical trials, regulatory strategy, manufacturing and commercialization.

Sources indicate that provide initial investments. The proposed PPP would not replace existing grant-based systems or market-driven innovation; rather, it would act as a complement by targeting disease areas in which market risks and incentives consistently fail to generate sufficient private investment. The approach could yield fresh therapies and reduce the cost of care to society while generating revenue from newly introduced products.

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

In the United States, we propose a federal investment of one billion dollars annually over ten years, directed to specific disease areas. That is less than 1.8% of total US government spending on biomedical research, which was $54.5 billion in 2024. This would be supplemented by smaller investments of 10–20% of one billion dollars from a consortium of philanthropic foundations and industry partners joining the initiative in response to a request for application. Given the high costs of bringing a newly introduced drug to market, a $10-billion total investment should provide the scale and time needed to pursue about three major disease targets10–12.

Feed revenues back in. Public return is a defining feature of the PPP. Existing biomedical funding structures are mainly grant making, with the implication that public benefit will emerge indirectly through the downstream health improvements and economic growth spurred by discovery. By contrast, this PPP framework would directly incorporate public accountability as well as returns.

According to recent reports, the government would need to leverage its status as a majority investor to ensure access, fair pricing and affordability. It might require conditions such as agreements to ensure access. Pricing frameworks could incorporate a value-based approach to pricing, in which health insurers offer reimbursements determined by a drug’s value for patients. Affordability conditions, such as reasonable-pricing clauses, would also serve as powerful leverage.

#198463. Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell
